Cc: Amit Rao <amit@kairos.ai>
Date: 2028-07-26T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Provisioning timeline and MAP for dedicated GPU pool

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Kairos Labs is excited to move toward a dedicated GPU pool for our inference-heavy workloads. To keep procurement and engineering aligned, I attached an initial mutual action plan (MAP) that sketches intake milestones, a preferred go-live window, and the SOW items we expect to finalize.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirmation on regional capacity options (we prefer primary US-West with EU failover).
- Autoscale/burst policy options and a recommended default for warm-burst behavior.
- An initial estimate for typical P95 latency at 2048-token sequences for the chosen instance family.

We have a tight Q3 window (targeting pilot in the second week of September). Could we schedule a 30–45 min alignment call next week to lock the MAP and SOW scope?

Attached: MAP_Kairos_v1.xlsx

Cheers,
Priya Singh
Head of Platform Partnerships
Kairos Labs

---

Note: MAP file lists high-level milestones and who owns each step. Happy to walk through details on the call.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@kairos.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-26T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisioning timeline and MAP for dedicated GPU pool

Thanks Priya — this is a great starting point. I'm available Tuesday or Thursday next week for a 30–45 minute alignment; propose Tuesday 10:00am PT or Thursday 2:00pm PT. Monica and Ben are looped in so we can confirm operational constraints.

Quick answers up front to your asks:
- Regional: US-West primary + EU (Frankfurt) failover is realistic; we'll confirm capacity SKU options once we validate your expected concurrency.
- Autoscale/burst: we typically recommend a warm-burst buffer (20–30% reserved GPU warm-standing capacity) plus dynamic burst to a pre-agreed ceiling. Monica will propose a conservative default based on your estimated QPS.
- Latency: rough P95 for 2048 tokens on an M40-family (quantized) path is ~180–220ms under continuous batching assumptions; we'll run a quick sim during onboarding to get a customer-specific profile.

Please find the MAP attached to this thread. If Tuesday 10am PT works, I'll send a calendar invite and an initial agenda: 1) finalize region/instance family 2) agree autoscale/burst policy 3) SOW items & signatures timeline.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-27T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Provisioning timeline and MAP for dedicated GPU pool

Internal note — drafting the conservative policy to propose to Kairos. Outline below for the call (I'll convert to slide bullets):

1) Baseline topology suggestion
- Primary pool: US-West (g4dn-like topology / 8xA10g equiv) sized for baseline concurrency of 40 vCPU-equivalent workers; initial reserved GPUs = 8
- Failover pool: EU-FRA warm standby with 2 reserved GPUs (cold-start fallback path on region failover)

2) Autoscale & burst policy (recommended defaults)
- Warm buffer: 25% of reserved (provides sub-250ms cold-start bounds for short spikes)
- Dynamic burst ceiling: +100% of reserved for up to 30 minutes per incident window (configurable; billable as burst usage)
- Prefetch/KV caching: enable prefix caching for 256-token common prompts to reduce per-token cost and tail latency

3) Operational guardrails
- Canary: 48h canary at 20% traffic shift
- Rollback: automatic fallback to hosted-compatible variant if quantization/regret metrics breach thresholds

4) Items for SOW (ownership split)
- Redwood: pool provisioning, autoscale rules, monitoring + 90-day performance tuning
- Kairos: app-side load shaping, integration of rollout hooks, SRE contact for netops VLAN peering

I'll bring this as the recommendation on the call. Marissa — can you confirm procurement timeline details so Jonas can include in the SOW dates?

—Monica
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Singh <psingh@kairos.ai>

Jonas / team —

Thanks for the quick internal alignment and the proposed defaults, Monica. The MAP looks good overall and our procurement team has penciled the Sept pilot window. A few clarifications before we lock SOW: 

1) Can you confirm how burst billing is reported? We need line items that separate reserved capacity vs burst consumption for our internal chargeback.
2) For the EU failover, do you support live replication of KV caches or do we accept a cold-warm cache rebuild on failover?
3) Please attach a draft SOW we can circulate to our legal/procurement; we prefer a 60-day review period.

Attaching: SOW_Kairos_draft.pdf (initial redline-ready version).

If everything looks OK we can route the SOW for signature; I'm including procurement lead Amit as a cc.

Best,
Priya

Subject: Re: Provisioning timeline and MAP for dedicated GPU pool

Priya / Amit —

Appreciate the speedy review. Answers inline and next steps below.

1) Burst billing: we will provide a detailed monthly usage statement that breaks out reserved monthly commitment (flat fee) and burst consumption (metered per-GPU-hour). We'll add a sample billing appendix to the SOW that shows the format and field names (line items: reserved_commitment_usd, burst_gpu_hours, burst_charge_usd).

2) KV cache replication: at this time we recommend a warm-failover model — live replication of in-memory prefix caches across regions is not enabled by default due to network consistency costs. During failover the EU pool will rebuild cold-warm cache; we can provide a pre-warm script and a short ramp window to mitigate tail latency. We'll add that behavior to the SOW and a small runbook item for failover rehearsals.

3) SOW: attached as requested. The file includes: scope, milestones aligned to the MAP, acceptance criteria, billing appendix, and a 60-day review & signature timeline. Link to DocuSign prep: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/link/abc123

Action items and timeline (proposed):
- By 2028-08-07: Kairos legal to provide any redlines to SOW (Amit)
- By 2028-08-14: Redwood to return final SOW for signature
- 2028-08-21: Signatures complete and technical kickoff scheduled
- 2028-09-09 — 2028-09-13: Pilot week (canary at 20% traffic)

Attachments: SOW_Kairos_draft.pdf, SOW_Kairos_signed_instructions.pdf (contains DocuSign steps for your procurement team).

I'll send a calendar invite for the Tuesday 10:00am PT call once Amit confirms availability. Thanks all — excited to get Kairos live.

Jonas Weber
